To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

waterpipe tobacco smoke is a respirabe inhalation hazard that contains significant concentrations of carcinogens, toxins and toxicants that cause heart disease, lung diseases and cancer in cigarette and waterpipe smokers.

waterpipe tobacco smoke is a respirabe aerosol that contains significant amounts of toxicants, including 27 known or suspect carcinogens; and that the same toxicants are present at similar levels in smoke produced from tobacco-free alternatives.

waterpipe smoking using sweet, flavoured tobacco or tobacco-free products generates smoke containing high doses of toxicants that cause disease in cigarette smokers, with similar cellular effects as cigarette smoke, and that the smoke is inhaled as an aerosol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical, physical and biologic properties of waterpipe tobacco smoking (WTS), a rapidly growing global public health concern.
the development of a mathematical model of the process of waterpipe tobacco smoking and its use in the analysis of experimental data.
the development of a mathematical model for the prediction of the concentration of a toxic gas in the waterpipe smoke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
waterpipe smoking is not a safe alternative to cigarette smoking.
waterpipe tobacco smoke is not less hazardous than cigarette smoke and that the health effects of waterpipe smoking are similar to cigarette smoking.
WTS and smoke generated using tobacco- free products marketed as ‘health conscious’ alternatives are not safe to inhale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the smoke from tobacco and non-tobacco waterpipes is a serious health hazard.
WTS contains significant amounts of toxicants and is a respirable, inhaled aerosol that induces responses associated with lung and heart diseases.
WTS is a significant health risk, and that tobacco-free products are not a safe alternative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
waterpipe smoking, like cigarette smoking, is a serious inhalation health hazard.

the toxicant and particle content, and biological activity of smoke generated from the most popular tobacco-free waterpipe preparations are not significantly different from those generated from conventional tobacco products.
the use of tobacco-free products does not reduce the toxicant content or the biological activity of WTS.
